Definition: from G4253 and G3191; to premeditate:--meditate before.
BiblicalUsage: Promeleteo means to premeditate, to practise beforehand. Jesus uses it once: settle it in your hearts not to meditate before what ye shall answer, for I will give you a mouth and wisdom.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the promise covers the unprepared moment, and the wisdom given then is better than any speech I rehearse now.
